## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Mic 2:1-13 is taken as a single reading unit: an indictment of premeditated land-seizure by the powerful (vv1-2), the LORD's matching verdict (vv3-5), a controversy with false prophets who deny any coming disgrace (vv6-7, 11), a specific bill of harms against "my people" (vv8-10), and a closing hope-oracle of regathering (vv12-13). "Bearing on the inner being" includes: (i) "those who devise wickedness" — the chapter's oppressor-collective, given the clearest premeditation-before-action content of the book so far; (ii) the LORD, matching their own verb back at them (v3); (iii) their specific individual victims ("a man and his house," v2; "the women... their young children," v9); (iv) the false prophets/complicit audience (vv6, 11); (v) "my people" (vv8-9, both the victims and, confusingly, the label under which the oppressors themselves are also addressed, v8); (vi) Jacob/the remnant of Israel, gathered in the closing hope-oracle (vv12-13); (vii) "their king"/the LORD, leading them out (v13).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (163/163 non-particle spans). Register shifts within the chapter: prophetic "woe"-oracle (vv1-2), divine first-person judgment introduced by "therefore thus says the LORD" (vv3-5), quoted false-prophetic speech and direct rebuttal (vv6-7), narrated indictment (vv8-10), a further quoted hypothetical false-preacher (v11), and a closing first-person divine hope-oracle (vv12-13).

**Corpus-continuity check.** Immediately-adjacent prior range, found automatically: `Mic 1:1-16` — `iba\app\verse-analysis\Micah\WA-mic-1-debate.md`. Read in full before drafting this debate. Carried forward: the divine-possessive "my people/my X" pattern (Mic 1:9, continuing an EQ from Joel/Obadiah); the LORD as the book's controlling operative agent; Jacob/house of Israel as the named guilty collective (Mic 1:5), here specified further as a party WITHIN which oppressor preys on victim (a narrowing from nation-level to intra-community guilt).

## Per-verse debate

### Mic 2:1

> Woe to those who devise wickedness and work evil on their beds! When the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand.

**Observation.** "Woe [H1945] to those who devise [H2803I] wickedness [H0205G] and work [H6466] evil [H7451B] on their beds [H4904]! When the morning [H1242] dawns [H0216], they perform [H6213A] it, because it is in the power [H0410L] of their hand [H3027G]."

**Operation 1 — premeditated wickedness, planned by night and executed at dawn.**
- **Action-type:** devised/performed (a two-stage operation: interior planning, then deliberate execution — the clearest illustration yet in this study of read-guidance step 1 note (a)'s "state precedes act" structure).
- **Subject:** "those who devise wickedness" — an unnamed human collective (note (c)), specified in v2 as those with the power to act on their plans (implicitly the landed/powerful).
- **Operation:** a state — the nighttime devising/planning itself, an explicitly stated interior act of premeditation; a movement — its dawn execution, deliberately timed.
- **Source:** self — "because it is IN THE POWER OF THEIR HAND," an explicit, direct statement that their capability to act is entirely self-sourced, not enabled or granted by an outside party (Part B.5's state-vs-enablement distinction directly and unusually cleanly answered within the verse itself).
- **Target:** n/a directly within this verse (the victims are named at v2).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Those who devise wickedness" — given the chapter's clearest possible stated interior content: not an outward act inviting inference, but explicit premeditation, named as such.
- Q3: Stated explicitly — "devise," "work," "perform" are all direct verbs of the subject's own action.
- Q4: Source of both the plan and the capacity to execute it = self, explicitly stated ("in the power of their hand") — an unusually direct case where the text itself forecloses any external-enablement reading.
- Q5: Target = n/a within this verse; supplied at v2.
- Q6: State (nighttime devising) and movement (dawn execution).
- Q7: **Major forward linkage — the chapter's clearest Q12 anchor.** The verb "devise" (H2803I) recurs at v3 with the LORD as its subject ("I am devising disaster"), a direct, deliberate lexical echo — flagged fully at v3.
- Q8: "Those who devise wickedness" — an unnamed collective, likely the powerful/landed class specified at v2.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the specific content of the "wickedness" is supplied at v2.
- Q11: devised/performed.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's opening operation, and the source of its central Q12 anchor at v3.

### Mic 2:2

> They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them away; they oppress a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

**Observation.** "They covet [H2530A] fields [H7704G] and seize [H1497] them, and houses [H1004B], and take them away [H5375G]; they oppress [H6231] a man [H1397] and his house [H1004B], a man [H0376G] and his inheritance [H5159]."

**Operation 1 — the specific content of v1's premeditated wickedness: coveting and seizing land and inheritance.**
- **Action-type:** coveted/seized/oppressed (a clean, explicit interior-desire-to-outward-act chain, illustrating read-guidance step 1 note (a) as directly as this study has yet found).
- **Subject:** the same oppressor-collective from v1; "a man and his house," "a man and his inheritance" — specific, individuated human victims, distinct from v1's abstract "wickedness."
- **Operation:** a state — coveting (H2530A, an interior desire, directly named, not inferred from the seizure that follows it); a movement — seizing, taking away, oppressing, the acted-out consequence of that desire.
- **Source:** self — the oppressors' own desire, continuing v1's explicit self-sourcing.
- **Target:** fields, houses (seized); "a man and his house," "a man and his inheritance" (oppressed) — real, individuated victims.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The oppressors — continuing v1's stated interior (desire, now specifically named "covet"). The victims ("a man," twice) — individuated human candidates (note (f)), given no stated interior of their own within this verse, only the fact of what is done to them.
- Q3: Stated explicitly throughout — desire, then act.
- Q4: Source = self (the oppressors' own coveting), explicit.
- Q5: Target = fields, houses, a man's house, a man's inheritance — real property and real persons.
- Q6: State (coveting) then movement (seizing, oppressing).
- Q7: **Forward linkage to v4** — the same domain (fields, portion/inheritance) recurs there as what the oppressors THEMSELVES will lose, a direct talionic reversal.
- Q8: N/A — the victims are individuated ("a man," singular, twice), not addressed as a collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: coveted (interior); seized/oppressed (acted-out).

**Decision.** Retain — the specific content of v1's premeditated wickedness, and the direct source of v4's coming reversal.

### Mic 2:3

> Therefore thus says the Lord: behold, against this family I am devising disaster, from which you cannot remove your necks, and you shall not walk haughtily, for it will be a time of disaster.

**Observation.** "Therefore thus says [H0559] the LORD [H3068G]: behold [H2005], against this [H2063] family [H4940] I am devising [H2803I] disaster [H7451C], from which you cannot [H3808] remove [H4185] your necks [H6677A], and you shall not [H3808] walk [H1980I] haughtily [H7317], for it will be a time [H6256] of disaster [H7451C]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's declared verdict, using the oppressors' own verb back against them.**
- **Action-type:** devised (identical action-type to v1's "devised," H2803I — the same Hebrew root, not merely a similar English gloss).
- **Subject:** the LORD, speaking in first person; "this family" — the oppressor-collective of vv1-2, now addressed directly as a body.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — a declared, inescapable coming disaster ("you cannot remove your necks," a yoke-image of inescapable subjugation), and a stated loss of status ("you shall not walk haughtily" — directly answering the very "power of their hand" self-confidence stated at v1).
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own declared act, explicitly causal ("therefore") from vv1-2's charge.
- **Target:** "this family" — the oppressors themselves.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "This family" — continuing as the addressed subject, now the recipient of a verdict rather than the actor.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, first-person divine declaration.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicit, directly causal from vv1-2.
- Q5: Target = the oppressors, their own necks, their own gait/bearing.
- Q6: State (the coming disaster) and movement (inability to walk haughtily any longer).
- Q7: **Q12 — Divine mirroring (anchored).** The LORD's "I am DEVISING [H2803I] disaster" directly, deliberately repeats the identical verb used of the oppressors' own premeditated "devising" (H2803I) of wickedness at v1 — not a suggestive resemblance but a shared lemma, the same word turned back on its own users, a clean textual anchor per read-guidance step 5 note (b)/Q12: the human operation (devising wickedness, v1) is directly inverted by a stated divine operation using the identical action-type (devising disaster, v3) — a talionic reversal comparable to Obadiah 15's "as you have done, it shall be done to you."
- Q8: "This family" — a collective, though a narrower, more intimate term than "nation" or "peoples" — suggesting an intra-community, not merely international, guilt (contrast Mic 1's Samaria/Jerusalem-level charges).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: devised (matching v1's action-type exactly).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's clearest, most directly textually-anchored Q12 instance: the LORD's own verdict phrased in the oppressors' own vocabulary.

### Mic 2:4

> In that day they shall take up a taunt song against you and moan bitterly, and say, “We are utterly ruined; he changes the portion of my people; how he removes it from me! To an apostate he allots our fields.”

**Observation.** "In that day [H3117G] they [H1931] shall take up [H5375N] a taunt [H4912] against you and moan [H5091] bitterly [H1961/H5092], and say [H0559]: 'We are utterly [H7703] ruined [H7703]; he changes [H4171] the portion [H2506A] of my people [H5971A]; how [H0349A] he removes [H4185] it from me! To an apostate [H7728] he allots [H2505A] our fields [H7704G].'"

**Operation 1 — the taunt-song quoting the oppressors' own future lament over their lost fields.**
- **Action-type:** lamented/mourned (a quoted future song of loss, directly reversing v2's own coveting/seizing of fields).
- **Subject:** an unnamed "they" (most naturally the oppressors of vv1-3, now themselves voicing loss, in a poetic-justice construction); the quoted speech's own first-person "we"/"my"/"our."
- **Operation:** a state — bitter mourning, quoted directly, over the very loss of "portion" and "fields" that vv1-2 described them seizing from others.
- **Source:** an unnamed "he" within the quoted lament — most plausibly the LORD, continuing v3's declared verdict, though not restated with an explicit divine subject within this verse's own grammar.
- **Target:** "the portion of my people," "our fields" — the oppressors' own former gains, now reallocated "to an apostate."

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The taunting/mourning "they" — given a genuinely stated future interior: bitter grief, quoted directly in first person within the song itself.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct quotation.
- Q4: Source of the reallocation = an unnamed "he," most plausibly the LORD (continuing v3), not explicitly restated as divine subject within this verse.
- Q5: Target = the oppressors' own former "portion"/"fields," reallocated to "an apostate."
- Q6: State (bitter mourning).
- Q7: **Direct linkage, talionic reversal**: v2 ("they covet fields and seize them") is directly answered by v4 (their own fields lost, reallocated). Also continues the divine-possessive pattern: "my people" (v4) — a further instance of the framing already tracked from Mic 1:9/Joel/Obadiah.
- Q8: "My people" — the same collective label used elsewhere for the LORD's own possession, here specifically the victims whose "portion" was changed.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the identity of "an apostate" (a specific individual, or a generic figure for whoever benefits from the reallocation) is not detailed — named as insufficiency.
- Q11: lamented/mourned.

**Decision.** Retain — a direct talionic reversal of v2, and a further instance of the divine-possessive "my people" pattern, carried forward as EQ.

### Mic 2:6

**Operation 1 — the false prophets' (or the resistant audience's) own quoted denial and self-reassurance.**
- **Action-type:** denied/preached-against (a quoted attempt to silence true prophecy, paired with an explicit, stated self-deception about coming consequence).
- **Subject:** an unnamed "they" — most plausibly a party resisting Micah's own message (whether false prophets or a wider complicit audience is not disambiguated within this verse), given the chapter's first explicitly quoted human speech.

- **Target:** the true prophetic message itself (suppressed); implicitly Micah/the LORD's own word.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**

### Mic 2:8

- **Subject:** "my people" — used here, strikingly, for the OPPRESSORS specifically, not their victims; "those who pass by trustingly" — unsuspecting, peaceable travellers, explicitly said to have "no thought of war," i.e. entirely undefended.
- **Operation:** a movement — rising up as an enemy against one's own; stripping outer garments (the "rich robe"/mantle, likely taken as security or plunder) from the defenceless.

- **Target:** the unsuspecting passers-by, stripped of their own clothing.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "My people" (as aggressor) — a genuinely stated, ironic reversal: the SAME collective-label used positively elsewhere (v4, Mic 1:9) here names the guilty party itself, a real interpretive tension worth flagging (Q8 below); the passers-by — individuated, undefended human victims (note (f)).

- Q8: "My people" used here for the guilty party specifically — a genuine tension with its use elsewhere (v4, Mic 1:9) for the LORD's own possession/the victims — the SAME label spans both victim and aggressor across this short passage, worth carrying forward as an emergent question about how this label functions across the book.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: turned-enemy/stripped.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's sharpest reversal, and the source of a genuine open question about "my people"'s shifting reference.

- **Action-type:** preferred/welcomed (a stated, biting irony: the people's own corrupted taste in what they will accept as "prophecy").
- **Subject:** a hypothetical "man" — not a real, named individual but a rhetorical construction (compare Obad 5's hypothetical thieves/gatherers), illustrating what "this people" actually wants; "this people," the collective whose own preference is exposed.
- **Operation:** a state — the hypothetical false preacher's own wind/lies (H7307H/H8267, "wind and lies" — an explicit charge of emptiness and deception); a state/reflection — the people's own readiness to accept exactly such a message, PROVIDED it promises indulgence (wine, strong drink) rather than judgment.
- **Source:** self — both the hypothetical preacher's own fabrication, and, more pointedly, the people's own corrupted appetite that would welcome it.
- **Target:** "this people" — themselves, reflexively exposed by the hypothetical's own logic.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The hypothetical "man" — set aside as a rhetorical device (step 3 note (a)), not a real candidate, exactly as Obad 5's hypothetical thieves were; "this people" — the verse's real, exposed subject: their own preference, not the hypothetical preacher's, is the actual point.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct hypothetical construction and direct quotation.
- Q4: Source = the people's own corrupted preference, self, explicit — the hypothetical merely exposes it.
- Q5: Target = reflexive — the people's own exposed taste.
- Q6: State throughout (a posed hypothetical exposing an existing preference, not a new enacted movement).
- Q7: Direct linkage to v6 (the same underlying dynamic — a comfortable falsehood preferred over the true, hard word) and to v7 (the true word, contrasted, "does good to him who walks uprightly").
- Q8: "This people" — a national collective, its own preference exposed.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: preferred/welcomed (the people's own exposed taste).

**Decision.** Set aside the hypothetical preacher as rhetorical device only (per step 3 note (a), matching Obad 5's precedent); retain "this people"'s own exposed preference as the verse's actual IB-bearing content.

### Mic 2:12

> I will surely assemble all of you, O Jacob; I will gather the remnant of Israel; I will set them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture, a noisy multitude of men.

**Observation.** "I will surely [H0622] assemble [H0622] all [H3605] of you, O Jacob [H3290]; I will gather [H6908] the remnant [H7611] of Israel [H3478]; I will set [H7760A] them together [H3162A] like [H9004] sheep [H6629G] in a fold [H1223], like [H9004] a flock [H5739] in the midst [H8432] of its pasture [H1699A], a noisy [H1949] multitude of men [H0120G]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's declared future regathering of Jacob/the remnant of Israel.**
- **Action-type:** gathered/assembled (a first-person divine declaration, an abrupt tonal shift from the preceding judgment material, using the same first-person "I will" register already established for both judgment (v3) and, now, restoration).
- **Subject:** the LORD, speaking in first person; "Jacob," "the remnant of Israel" — the whole covenant people, here addressed as recipients of promised restoration rather than charged with guilt.
- **Operation:** a movement — gathering, assembling; a state — being set together in safety and abundance, likened to a well-populated, noisy flock in good pasture (a deliberate image of security and increase, contrasting the chapter's earlier images of loss and expulsion).
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own declared future act.
- **Target:** Jacob, the remnant of Israel — gathered together.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jacob/the remnant of Israel — given here a stated future condition of safety and abundance, a sharp contrast to vv1-11's judgment and loss.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, first-person divine declaration.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = Jacob/the remnant, gathered.
- Q6: Movement (gathering) and state (secure abundance).
- Q7: **A genuine, unresolved tonal fork.** This verse's abrupt shift from judgment (vv1-11) to hope is not explained by this passage's own data — whether it is the LORD's own genuine, separate declaration (the reading taken here, on the strength of the same first-person "I will" register already used at v3 for judgment) or bears some other relationship to the false-preaching just exposed at v11 is not resolved by the text itself — named as an open interpretive question, not settled here (see insufficiencies register).
- Q8: "Jacob," "the remnant of Israel" — the whole covenant collective, now the object of restoration rather than charge.
- Q9: Insufficient — the reason for the abrupt judgment-to-hope shift is not supplied by this passage's own data.
- Q11: gathered/assembled.

**Decision.** Retain, read as the LORD's own genuine declaration on the strength of its shared first-person register with v3 — the tonal shift itself flagged as an open, unresolved question, not smoothed over.

### Mic 2:13

> He who opens the breach goes up before them; they break through and pass the gate, going out by it. Their king passes on before them, the Lord at their head.

**Observation.** "He who opens the breach [H6555] goes up [H5927G] before [H6440G] them; they break through [H6555] and pass [H5674A] the gate [H8179G], going out [H3318G] by it. Their king [H4428G] passes on [H5674A] before [H6440G] them, the LORD [H3068G] at their head [H7218I]."

**Operation 1 — the Breaker leading the regathered flock out through the gate, with their king/the LORD at their head.**
- **Action-type:** led-out (a triumphant, closing image of deliverance — a figure who "opens the breach," the flock following through the broken gate, and a final identification of "their king" with the LORD himself, both said to be "at their head").
- **Subject:** "he who opens the breach" — an unnamed leader-figure (human or divinely-appointed, not disambiguated within this base extract's own data); "they" — the regathered flock of v12; "their king," directly paired/identified with "the LORD" in the same closing clause.
- **Operation:** a movement — ascending, breaking through, passing the gate, going out — a deliberate reversal of vv9-10's own images of expulsion FROM houses/land; here, a movement OUT that is triumphant, led, not driven.
- **Source:** self — the Breaker's own leading act; the LORD's own leadership, explicitly named at the verse's close.
- **Target:** n/a directly — the flock's own deliverance, not an external target.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "He who opens the breach" — an unnamed candidate, possibly human (a leader), possibly a divine title, not disambiguated; the flock — the same regathered collective from v12, now given a movement of deliverance rather than a static state of safety.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as direct declarative narrative.
- Q4: Source = the Breaker's own leading act; ultimately "the LORD at their head" — the two roles ("their king" and "the LORD") placed in direct apposition, raising a genuine question of whether they are identified as one and the same or presented as two figures acting together — named as insufficiency/interpretive fork, not resolved here.
- Q5: N/A directly.
- Q6: Movement throughout.
- Q7: **Closing linkage, chapter-bracketing reversal.** vv9-10's images of forced expulsion (women driven from houses, the land itself vomiting out its inhabitants) are directly answered by this verse's image of a LED, triumphant going-out — the same basic movement (leaving one's place) transformed from judgment to deliverance.
- Q8: "They" — the regathered flock, a maximal covenant collective, given a share in the Breaker's own leading movement.
- Q9: Insufficient — the identity of "he who opens the breach" (a specific historical/eschatological figure, or a general image for divinely-appointed leadership) and the precise relationship between "their king" and "the LORD" are not resolved by this base extract's own data.
- Q11: led-out.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's closing operation, directly reversing vv9-10's images of forced expulsion into a led, triumphant deliverance; the Breaker's identity and the king/LORD relationship both carried forward as open questions.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The chapter's central Q12 instance (v1 → v3)**: "devise" (H2803I) used first of the oppressors' own premeditated wickedness, then of the LORD's own matching verdict — a direct, textually-anchored talionic reversal, the clearest such instance in this study's reading of Micah so far.
2. **The fields/portion/inheritance thread**: v2 (oppressors covet and seize fields) → v4 (their own fields lost, reallocated "to an apostate") → v5 (permanently excluded from the assembly's own land-lottery) — one continuous vocabulary domain carrying the whole judgment section.
3. **The expulsion-reversed-to-deliverance thread**: v9 (women driven from their own houses) / v10 (a commanded departure, "no place to rest") → v13 (a LED, triumphant going-out through a broken gate) — the same basic movement (leaving one's place) transformed across the chapter from judgment to hope.
4. **The false-preaching thread**: v6 (a quoted denial: "disgrace will not overtake us") → v7 (direct rebuttal) → v11 (the people's own exposed preference for a lying, indulgent preacher) — one sustained controversy over true vs. false prophecy.
5. **"My people"'s unstable reference**: used for the LORD's own possession and the judgment's victims (v4's "my people," v9's "the women of my people") AND, strikingly, for the oppressors themselves as the ones who "rise up as an enemy" against their own (v8) — the same label spanning both victim and aggressor within a few verses, carried forward as an emergent question.
6. **The divine-possessive pattern, continuing**: "my people" (v4, v8, v9), "my splendor" (v9) — now four instances within this single chapter alone, on top of the cross-book pattern already tracked from Mic 1:9/Joel/Obadiah.
7. **The unresolved judgment-to-hope pivot (vv1-11 → vv12-13)**: not explained by this passage's own data; read here as the LORD's own genuine declaration on the strength of its shared first-person register with v3, but flagged, not smoothed over, as a genuine open question.

## Insufficiencies register

- The precise composition of the "they" who deny coming disgrace (v6) — false prophets specifically, or a wider complicit audience — is not disambiguated by this base extract.
- The identity of "an apostate" (v4), to whom the oppressors' own fields are reallocated, is not named.
- Whether v10's commanded departure is addressed to the same oppressor-collective charged throughout the chapter, or more generally to the land's inhabitants, is not fully disambiguated within the verse itself.
- The reason for the chapter's abrupt shift from sustained judgment (vv1-11) to a hope-oracle of regathering (vv12-13) is not supplied by this passage's own data — read here as the LORD's own genuine declaration (shared first-person register with v3), but not confirmed or explained by the text itself.
- The identity of "he who opens the breach" (v13) — a specific figure, historical or eschatological, or a general image of divinely-appointed leadership — is not resolved.
- The precise relationship between "their king" and "the LORD," placed in direct apposition at v13's close, is not disambiguated — identity, or two figures acting together, both remain open.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** "My people" now spans BOTH the victims (v4, v9) and the aggressors (v8) within a single short passage — worth testing against how this label functions elsewhere in the book (and the corpus) once more chapters/books are read: is this a deliberate rhetorical instability, or does context always eventually disambiguate it?
- **EQ2.** The judgment-to-hope pivot at vv11→12 is abrupt and textually unexplained. Worth watching whether Micah's remaining chapters supply further data that clarifies this pattern, rather than assuming a scholarly-traditional explanation not supplied by the base extract itself.
- **EQ3.** The Breaker/king/LORD figure of v13 — worth comparing, once the rest of Micah is read, against any further messianic/royal figures that may recur.
- **EQ4.** The chapter's Q12 instance (v1/v3, "devise") is a clean, single-word talionic reversal — a distinct, more compact SHAPE of divine-mirroring than Obadiah's extended "as you have done, it shall be done to you" construction. Worth tracking, once more of the corpus is read, whether single-verb echo-verdicts recur as their own recognisable sub-pattern of Q12.

## Open decisions / next steps

- The oppressor-collective's precise social identity (landed elite, local officials, or a wider class) is not further specified by this base extract; left open rather than assumed from outside historical knowledge.
